alerts.detail:
On August 28th, 2011 Hurricane Irene struck New England. The resulting floods caused extensive damage throughout the region, the worst in over 100 years. More than half the rivers in Vermont and northern New Hampshire recorded their highest flow levels ever. Many roads, guardrails, power lines, bridges, trees and other debris now litter several rivers throughout the region. River beds have been scoured and changed course, many new strainers make navigation problematic at best and downright dangerous at worse. Please realize that the river description you see here may not match current situation after the floods. Use common sense and when in doubt scout especially on blind drops. Also, if you run this river in the next year or so please comment on its navigability, even if there are no problems this will be very helpful. Please report any new strainers or changes to the rapids that will impact future boating.
Thank you,

detail.description:
Stone Church Put-In (upper): Access the river close to the route 3 intersection (park behind St. Patrick's Church). The first 2 miles are good for a Class I / II warm up before encountering the continuous class II waters below.

Rest Area Put-In (lower): To bypass the extended warm-up section above, find the rest area on state route 302 about two miles west from the intersection of state route 3 in Twin Mountain. Look for a convenient riverside paved pull off across from Beechwood Drive.

From the Rest Area Put-In: the river starts with typical boulder strewn class II sections that wend around corners. Look for lots of small play waves and eddies. The first major rapid is Fish Camp Rapid, where the river narrows over class II ledge drops and small holes to dodge. After several quickwater sections alternating with boulder strewn sections, the river gradient increases and comes to a more difficult class II+ section called Boat Breaker just about a half mile upstream of the take out at Pierce Bridge. There is a clear path through river center with some left and right zig-zags to avoid the larger holes. It is easy to boat-scout from resting eddies above each steep portion of this section. The take out is found on the immediate river right after the large concrete abuttments of Pierce Bridge.

Most of the river is secluded and out of site of the road with tall northern spruce along the banks. There are occasional camps along the way.

### Technical info

